hot.title: RoboDojo: A Unified Sim-and-Real Benchmark for Comprehensive Evaluation of Generalist Robot Manipulation Policies
hot.summary: RoboDojo establishes a unified sim-and-real benchmark for evaluating generalist robot manipulation policies, integrating 60 tasks across five capabilities for efficient simulation and reproducible real-world validation. An extensive evaluation of 30 policies using this benchmark reveals a substantial performance gap to human experts and identifies critical limitations in areas like precision, generalization, and open-semantic understanding.

hot.title: Vision Pretraining for Dense Spatial Perception
hot.summary: Robbyant researchers introduced masked boundary modeling, a self-supervised pretraining method for Vision Transformers that explicitly targets fine-grained spatial structure. The approach enabled a 1.1B parameter model to achieve an RMSE of 0.296 on NYU-Depth v2, surpassing larger models like the 7B DINOv3, and demonstrated leading performance in video object segmentation and depth completion.

hot.title: EdgeBench: Unveiling Scaling Laws of Learning from Real-World Environments
hot.summary: A precise log-sigmoid scaling law governing the performance improvement of large language model agents from interaction in real-world environments was identified, exhibiting a mean R² of 0.998 on the new EdgeBench benchmark and revealing that frontier agent learning speed doubled every three months.

hot.title: ResearchStudio-Idea: An Evidence-Grounded Research-Ideation Skill Suite from ML Conference Outcomes
hot.summary: ResearchStudio-Idea introduces an evidence-grounded skill suite, IdeaSpark, that extracts 15 operational ideation patterns from ML conference outcomes to guide large language models in generating high-quality research proposals. In an automated-judge study, IdeaSpark-generated ideas achieved a mean quality score of 3.87/4, ranking first in 88% of cases and maintaining competitive novelty compared to baseline LLMs.

hot.title: Harness Engineering for Self-Improvement
Is One Layer Enough? Training A Single Transformer Layer Can Match Full-Parameter RL Training
hot.summary: A study of large language model adaptation via reinforcement learning finds that performance gains are primarily concentrated in a stable subset of middle transformer layers, with single-layer training sometimes recovering over 100% of full-parameter training improvements and enabling more efficient training strategies.

hot.title: Gemma 4 Technical Report
hot.summary: Google DeepMind's Gemma 4 model family introduces open-weight, natively multimodal models capable of processing text, images, and audio. It demonstrates competitive performance across various benchmarks, including a 1451 Elo score on Arena Text for its 31B variant, while featuring enhanced efficiency, robust long-context understanding up to 256k tokens, and improved safety performance.

hot.title: UI-MOPD: Multi-Platform On-Policy Distillation for Continual GUI Agent Learning
hot.summary: Niu Lian et al. developed UI-MOPD, a multi-teacher on-policy distillation framework designed for continually learning GUI agents capable of operating across heterogeneous desktop and mobile platforms. The method achieved interactive task success rates of 38.2% on OSWorld and 12.0% on MobileWorld, outperforming baseline integration strategies and maintaining static GUI understanding and grounding capabilities.

hot.title: LLM-as-a-Verifier: A General-Purpose Verification Framework
hot.summary: Researchers from Stanford, UC Berkeley, and NVIDIA Research developed LLM-as-a-Verifier, a training-free framework that leverages fine-grained logit distributions for continuous feedback, demonstrating state-of-the-art performance in agentic tasks across coding, robotics, and medicine, while also improving reinforcement learning sample efficiency.

hot.title: PixWorld: Unifying 3D Scene Generation and Reconstruction in Pixel Space
hot.summary: PixWorld introduces a unified pixel-space diffusion framework that directly optimizes a 3D Gaussian Splatting representation for both 3D scene generation and reconstruction. This method leverages a two-stream Diffusion Transformer and a geometry perception loss, achieving state-of-the-art performance in novel-view synthesis and scene generation quality with improved geometric faithfulness across multiple benchmarks.

hot.title: Reinforcement learning towards broadly and persistently beneficial models
InternVLA-A1.5: Unifying Understanding, Latent Foresight, and Action for Compositional Generalization
hot.summary: InternVLA-A1.5, developed by the Physical Intelligence Team at Shanghai AI Laboratory, unifies understanding, latent foresight, and action for robotic control by employing a "latent-querying" approach to future prediction, where learnable tokens distill dynamics from a frozen pretrained video model. This framework improves compositional generalization and long-horizon execution on real-world and simulation benchmarks while maintaining real-time inference.

hot.title: CompactionRL: Reinforcement Learning with Context Compaction for Long-Horizon Agents
hot.summary: CompactionRL, a reinforcement learning framework developed by researchers at Tsinghua University and Z.AI, trains LLM agents to perform context compaction. This enables agents to effectively handle long-horizon interactive tasks, achieving an 8.0 point absolute increase in Pass@1 on SWE-bench Verified for a 30B parameter model compared to standard RL, by jointly optimizing task execution and summary generation within a fixed context window.

hot.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
hot.summary: The "Program-as-Weights" (PAW) paradigm allows developers to define "fuzzy functions" using natural language, which are then compiled into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts. A Qwen3-0.6B interpreter running PAW programs achieved 73.78% exact match accuracy on the FuzzyBench dataset, outperforming a Qwen3-32B model (68.70%) while utilizing approximately 50 times less inference memory.

hot.title: AutoMem: Automated Learning of Memory as a Cognitive Skill
hot.summary: AUTOMEM introduces a framework enabling Large Language Models to automatically learn and optimize memory management as a cognitive skill, rather than a fixed architectural component. By iteratively refining memory structures and training a specialized memory component, the system significantly improves agent performance on long-horizon tasks, achieving 1.89x to 3.74x gains in progression rate and making open-weight models competitive with frontier proprietary systems.

hot.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Direct On-Policy Distillation
hot.summary: Direct On-Policy Distillation (Direct-OPD) is a method that transfers reinforcement learning-induced policy shifts from smaller, weaker models to stronger, larger language models. This approach efficiently improves reasoning capabilities, achieving up to a 14.1 percentage point increase in accuracy on AIME benchmarks for student models and outperforming direct RL on larger models with significantly less computational cost.

hot.title: A Mathematical Introduction to Diffusion Models
hot.summary: Jianfeng Lu's mathematical introduction to diffusion models unifies classical sampling dynamics with modern score-based generative processes, presenting a comprehensive, proof-oriented framework. It rigorously derives core concepts like reverse-time SDEs and probability flow ODEs, provides a detailed error analysis for diffusion samplers, and extends the theoretical understanding to discrete data and inference-time control.

hot.title: DSpark: Confidence-Scheduled Speculative Decoding with Semi-Autoregressive Generation
hot.summary: DSpark proposes a confidence-scheduled speculative decoding framework employing semi-autoregressive generation to enhance LLM inference. This method improves draft quality for longer sequences and optimizes target model resource allocation, yielding 51% higher aggregate throughput and 60%–85% faster per-user generation speeds in production serving environments.

hot.title: Wan-Streamer v0.2: Higher Resolution, Same Latency
hot.summary: Wan-Streamer v0.2 enhances real-time audio-visual interaction by increasing output resolution from 192x336 to 640x368 pixels while preserving an approximate 200 ms model-side latency. This allows for more detailed close-up interactions and legible scene-grounded mid-shot digital agents within a 25 FPS stream.

hot.title: Multi-Turn On-Policy Distillation with Prefix Replay
hot.summary: Microsoft Research and University of Amsterdam developed ReOPD (Replayed-Prefix On-Policy Distillation), an efficient offline framework for training large language model agents in multi-turn interactive tasks. The method reduced training time per step by at least 4x and eliminated environment interactions, while matching or improving performance over online on-policy distillation, particularly for tasks with larger teacher-student capability gaps.

likes.title: LeVLJEPA: End-to-End Vision-Language Pretraining Without Negatives
likes.summary: LeVLJEPA presents a non-contrastive end-to-end vision-language pretraining method that forgoes negative pairs, yielding visual encoders with enhanced dense semantic features. The approach improves performance on semantic segmentation and as a frozen backbone for vision-language models, also demonstrating batch-size invariance.

likes.title: Next-Generation Agentic Reinforcement Learning Systems Enable Self-Evolving Agents
likes.summary: Researchers from Ant Group, HKUST, and Tsinghua University introduce a comprehensive system architecture designed to enable self-evolving LLM agents at an enterprise scale. This architecture proposes a standardized data protocol, an enterprise-grade data proxy, and a unified evolution control plane, with a prototype implementation (AREAL2.0) demonstrating online policy LLM weight updates from deployed agent interactions.

likes.title: WorldDirector: Building Controllable World Simulators with Persistent Dynamic Memory
likes.summary: WorldDirector, a framework from HKUST and Ant Group, allows for building controllable video world simulators by explicitly decoupling semantic motion orchestration from visual generation. This approach ensures persistent dynamic object memory, maintaining consistent visual identity and physical logic for entities even after prolonged periods outside the camera's view, and facilitates unrestricted viewpoint exploration.

likes.title: ABot-M0.5: Unified Mobility-and-Manipulation World Action Model
likes.summary: ABot-M0.5 unifies mobility and manipulation within a World Action Model by addressing structural misalignments in temporal granularity, action space, and train-test consistency. The model achieves state-of-the-art performance on mobile manipulation benchmarks and demonstrates effective transfer to real-world robotic systems with limited demonstrations.

likes.title: Denser≠\neq=Better: Limits of On-Policy Self-Distillation for Continual Post-Training
likes.summary: On-policy self-distillation (SDPO) for continual LLM post-training offers strong in-domain specialization but exhibits increased forgetting and instability in sequential learning scenarios, a consequence of dense token-level supervision's sensitivity to teacher dynamics and artifact amplification, contrasting with more stable sequence-level reward methods.

likes.title: Measuring the Gap Between Human and LLM Research Ideas
likes.summary: Researchers at Yale and University of Chicago quantified the qualitative differences between research ideas generated by Large Language Models (LLMs) and human scientists, revealing that LLMs exhibit a significantly narrower "research taste". LLMs disproportionately generate "bridge-and-synthesis" ideas, showing a distinct pattern compared to the broader distribution of human-conceived research directions.

likes.title: Representation Distribution Matching for One-Step Visual Generation
likes.summary: Researchers systematically dissect Representation Distribution Matching (RDM) for one-step visual generation, identifying optimal design choices including a robust MMD estimation, large generated batch sizes, and a multi-encoder strategy with constrained optimization. The improved RDM (iRDM) achieves new state-of-the-art on ImageNet-256 for one-step generation and successfully post-trains FLUX.2 into a superior one-step text-to-image model, with its samples preferred over held-out real photographs in 63.6% of comparisons.

likes.title: Purified OPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation Without Losing How to Think
likes.summary: Researchers from Zhejiang University and Alibaba Group diagnosed that standard On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) fails in long Chain-of-Thought (long-CoT) models due to non-transferable supervision. They developed Purified OPSD (OPSD-PMI), which isolates and leverages only inference-transferable knowledge, leading to consistent performance improvements across various LLMs on mathematical reasoning tasks while preserving their reflective thinking capabilities.

likes.title: VLA-Corrector: Lightweight Detect-and-Correct Inference for Adaptive Action Horizon
likes.summary: VLA-Corrector enhances the robustness of action-chunked Vision-Language-Action policies by introducing an inference-time framework that enables an adaptive action horizon and guided recovery. It improved average success rates by 15.65 percentage points on MetaWorld tasks for one VLA backbone and demonstrated a 17.7 percentage point increase in real-world robotic arm tasks, particularly in disturbance recovery.

likes.title: Perceive-to-Reason: Decoupling Perception and Reasoning for Fine-Grained Visual Reasoning
likes.summary: A framework called Perceive-to-Reason (P2R) is introduced, decoupling visual perception from linguistic reasoning in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) through a two-stage process. Trained with Perception-Reasoning Alternating GRPO (PRA-GRPO), this approach consistently improved fine-grained visual reasoning by up to 11.0% on high-resolution benchmarks and showed gains on general multimodal tasks, without requiring bounding box annotations.

likes.title: QuasiMoTTo: Quasi-Monte Carlo Test-Time Scaling
likes.summary: QuasiMoTTo introduces a method for generating batches of correlated, yet marginally exact, samples from large language models, addressing inefficiencies in current i.i.d. sampling. This approach demonstrated a 25-47% reduction in required samples for test-time inference scaling across reasoning benchmarks and enabled policy-gradient reinforcement learning to reach target performance with 50% fewer training steps.

likes.title: Learning to Move Before Learning to Do: Task-Agnostic pretraining for VLAs
likes.summary: A framework called Task-Agnostic Pretraining (TAP) teaches Vision-Language-Action models fundamental physical competence from abundant unlabeled data using inverse dynamics, then grounds these priors with minimal expert demonstrations. This approach achieved an average success rate of 33.32% on the SIMPLER benchmark, outperforming foundational models trained on limited expert data, and demonstrated enhanced robustness in real-world scenarios.

likes.title: PointDiT: Pixel-Space Diffusion for Monocular Geometry Estimation
likes.summary: PointDiT introduces a minimalist pixel-space diffusion framework for estimating dense 3D point maps from single RGB images, bypassing the architectural complexities of latent diffusion models and intricate loss functions of deterministic regressors. The model sets new benchmarks in depth accuracy and boundary sharpness, achieving efficient single-step inference while providing sharper geometric details than prior approaches.

likes.title: World from Motion: Generative Dynamic Gaussian Reconstruction from Monocular Video
likes.summary: The research by Stanford University and NVIDIA presents "World from Motion," a framework that unifies geometry-driven 4D reconstruction with generative modeling to create freely renderable dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting representations from monocular video. It achieves state-of-the-art performance on DyCheck (e.g., 19.78 mPSNR) and MultiCamVideo benchmarks (e.g., 27.43 PSNR) by distilling novel views from a 4D-conditioned video generator into a refined 4D scene model.

likes.title: Structured 4D Latent Predictive Model for Robot Planning
likes.summary: Researchers at MIT and Harvard developed a Structured 4D Latent Predictive Model, which learns and predicts the 3D structure and dynamics of a scene in a compact latent space for robot planning. This framework achieved an average 61.3% success rate on complex ManiSkill3 manipulation tasks, significantly outperforming 2D video-generative baselines, and demonstrated robust zero-shot generalization to novel visual conditions.

likes.title: PACE: A Proxy for Agentic Capability Evaluation
likes.summary: The PACE framework enables efficient and accurate prediction of large language model agent performance on costly agentic benchmarks by leveraging a small, automatically selected set of inexpensive non-agentic evaluation instances. This approach achieved an average LOOCV Mean Absolute Error of 3.80% for absolute performance prediction and 84.37% pairwise ranking accuracy, reducing evaluation costs by approximately 100 times compared to direct agentic evaluation.
